terminologyProfile.descriptionRule: Use measurable 3D graphics terms. Avoid vague words unless they are paired with concrete geometry/material/shader parameters.

referenceCamera.note: For likeness work, solve the reference camera (forge/stage1_intake/solve_camera_pose.py) so the review render aligns with the photo and the reference can be projected. Confirm by overlay review.

objectClass.notes: Static single-storey branded retail box on thaikit's shared 8.0 x 4.6 x 7.0 m module, exterior shell only. No interior geometry: glazing is a tinted mostly-opaque pane, not an opening. Nothing moves, so one root pivot and zero sockets is the correct contract. A filling-station forecourt kiosk, and structurally the odd one out in the retail set: what reads as a separate canopy is the building's OWN roof slab extending forward over the pump apron on two square columns. A navy fascia band with a red stripe under it wraps the slab edge on all three exposed sides and carries the ptt mark on the face that fronts the street. The building itself -- white render, one wide shopfront, a flush service door on +X, three condensers on the roof behind a parapet -- occupies only the REAR of the declared module.

reasoning: Silhouette is a single rectangular prism -- low geometric complexity.
Richness is REPETITION and PANELLING, not intricate form. The instanced systems collapse the repeated parts into one InstancedMesh each.
Occlusion risk is real: the rear elevation is entirely unseen in the single plate.
Action readiness is minimal: static exterior shell, box collider, not breakable.

specDepthDecision.rationale: Repetition-dominated facade: without repetitionSystems the mullion and plant sets would each cost a draw call per part and blow maxDrawCalls=12.

detailInventory.note: Enumerate every identity-defining small detail before authoring the spec. Each detail must map to a component.localFeatures entry or material.localOverrides entry, never prose only. Use forge/stage1_intake/build_detail_inventory.py to scan zones.

resolvedUnknowns: Rear (-Z) elevation is unobserved; authored plain. Confidence 0.20.
The pumps, apron and forecourt paving are NOT modelled. This asset is the kiosk and its canopy; the apron is the level builder's ground plane.
The plate shows a shop interior through the glazing. Not modelled: this prop is an exterior shell.
The plate's canopy overhangs further forward than 3.2 m relative to the building. Compressed to fit the declared 7.0 m depth, which is what pushes the shell back to z=0.30.

preSpecAssessment.unknownsResolutionNote: Emptied because every entry has been RESOLVED with a recorded authoring decision, not because the gaps went away. Each is restated in assumptions and in viewEvidence with its confidence and a null path. Nothing was invented to close a gap.

definitionOfDone: Rendered model matches the reference silhouette, the 8.0 x 4.6 x 7.0 m proportions, the visible component hierarchy and the material response for a real-time browser prop.
All four scene-budget ceilings hold: <=16000 triangles, <=12 draw calls, <=8 materials, <=16 unique geometries.
Zero coincident co-facing surface pairs (check-coplanar clean).
Exactly one root pivot and zero sockets; box collider; no destruction groups.
Every material declares textureless with named evidence.

visualAcceptance.scoringRule: AI vision must inspect a side-by-side reference/render sheet and score the current pass from 0 to 1. Pixel-diff code may assist diagnostics but cannot approve a pass.

featureReviewPolicy.selectionRule: Choose only the most visually salient, identity-defining, user-prioritized, or high-risk semantic systems. Group repeated parts instead of reviewing every mesh. AI vision scores every selected feature from the same full reference/render pair.

codeRefineTriggers: spec is adequate but generated geometry/material does not match
lighting hides geometry or material response
stopCriteria: target fidelity reached or user accepts current approximation

screenshotPolicy.minimumEvidence: Each visual pass needs a reference image, rendered screenshot, side-by-side comparison sheet, AI vision score, layer scores, and critique before choosing continue.
screenshotPolicy.reviewPairRule: Compare the same camera/viewpoint whenever possible; do not judge a front reference against a random render angle.
screenshotPolicy.acceptanceAuthority: AI vision review of the comparison sheet. Code-generated pixel similarity is not sufficient evidence.

referencePbrExtraction.acceptedLimitation: single-image extraction is reference-derived inference, not exact photogrammetry

mustAvoid: plastic-looking smooth bark, stone, cloth, foliage, or aged material
local color/detail described only in prose without material masks
claiming exact PBR recovery when confidence is below the target threshold
reference lighting copied without separating material readability

screenshotReview: Compare albedo palette and local color zones.
Compare cavity dirt, edge wear, stains, moss, scratches, or other local masks.
Compare key/fill/rim structure, exposure, tone mapping, background, and contact shadows.
Capture a neutral-light render to verify material readability without reference lighting.
Capture a grazing-light close-up to expose flat normals, uniform roughness, tiling, and plastic highlights.
Capture a reference-matched render from the same camera framing as the source.

pivotInventory.name: root
pivotInventory.justification: The ONLY mechanism this prop has. Nothing opens, turns or swings; doors and shutters are authored as fixed geometry, so they get no axis. A named pivot is a promise that a part turns on it.

actionReadiness.socketJustification: ZERO sockets, deliberately. Nothing attaches to this prop and nothing is emitted from it. A marker named for a place on the surface is a location, not a mechanism.

colliderInventory.note: The asset declares collider 'box'. One box proxy.

actionReadiness.destructionJustification: The asset declares destructionGroups as an empty list -- this prop is NOT breakable. No component carries actionProfile.destruction.fractureGroup. promote-model checks built against declared as an equality in BOTH directions, so an invented group fails the gate just as a missing one would.

assumptions: Rear (-Z) elevation is unobserved; authored plain. Confidence 0.20.
The pumps, apron and forecourt paving are NOT modelled. This asset is the kiosk and its canopy; the apron is the level builder's ground plane.
The plate shows a shop interior through the glazing. Not modelled: this prop is an exterior shell.
The plate's canopy overhangs further forward than 3.2 m relative to the building. Compressed to fit the declared 7.0 m depth, which is what pushes the shell back to z=0.30.
The ptt flame glyph is set as a typographic mark rather than the exact corporate droplet; the plate's own artwork is not reproduced.

coordinateFrame.notes: Origin base-center as the asset declares. The shopfront and the marked fascia face +Z. Because the canopy takes the front 3.2 m of the 7.0 m depth, the shell face is set BACK to z=0.30 rather than pushed forward like every sibling; that setback is the single most consequential geometric decision in this prop.

silhouette.description: Not a prism: a low slab floating forward on two columns, with the enclosed volume behind and above it. The silhouette events are the two columns, the deep undercut between the slab and the ground, the parapet capping the rear volume, and three condensers behind it.
silhouette.envelopeDerivation: x spans -4.00..+4.00 (parapet ring outer faces) = 8.00. y spans 0.00..4.60 = 4.60. z spans -3.50 (rear parapet) ..+3.50 = 7.00. The shell front face is set back to z=+2.50 so anything cantilevering off it lands ON the declared depth rather than overrunning it.
silhouette.meshyCrossCheck: Independent Meshy v7 reconstruction of the same plate normalises to w:h:d = 1 : 0.596 : 1.254 against the declared 1 : 0.575 : 0.875 -- height within 4%, but 43% deeper. The height agreement is the meaningful half: the proxy and the declaration agree about what this building IS. The depth divergence is the forecourt: the plate frames the canopy and its apron as part of the object, and the declared 7.0 m module is the kit's shared retail depth. The declaration wins and the canopy is fitted inside it at 3.2 m, which is why the shell is set back rather than the canopy being cropped.

viewEvidence.note: NOT OBSERVED. Authored as plain render with the parapet returning and no openings.

componentTree.name: Building shell
componentTree.topologyRationale: One continuous render skin over four walls. Splitting it per elevation would cost a draw call per wall for the life of the prop to express one material.

geometryDescriptor.topologyIntent: Solid box, x -3.94..+3.94, y 0..3.55, z -3.44..+2.50. SOLID, not a ring: the prop is an exterior shell only ever seen from outside, so an interior would cost draw calls, geometries and VRAM for something nobody sees. Solid also means the shopfront needs no opening cut in it, which removes all four reveal faces and the z-fighting they cause.
geometryDescriptor.zFightingNote: Set 0.06 m INSIDE the parapet ring on every elevation (walls at +-3.94 and -3.44; parapet at +-4.00 and -3.50). That difference is a coping drip edge, and it is what stops a wall face and a parapet face being coplanar and co-facing.

colorMaterialRecipe.recipe: Flat painted cement render, roughness 0.88, no texture set. Set BACK to z=0.30 so the canopy has the front 3.2 m of the declared depth.

pivot.name: root
pivot.notes: base-center, as the asset declares. A STATIC exterior shell: nothing opens, turns or swings, so one root pivot is the whole mechanism inventory and that is the correct answer, not a gap.

collider.notes: Declared on the asset as box. One convex proxy over the whole envelope; a level builder collides with the building, not with its canopy plates.

componentTree.name: Roof deck
componentTree.topologyRationale: A flat deck plane. Its own component only because the membrane is a visibly different value from the wall render, and this prop is seen from above in every hero shot.

geometryDescriptor.topologyIntent: Thin slab spanning y 3.50..3.62, overlapping UNDER the parapet ring.
geometryDescriptor.zFightingNote: Spans y 3.50..3.62 so its underside is sunk INTO the shell rather than resting on it. Authored flush, the deck bottom face and the parapet ring bottom face would both sit at y=3.550 facing down -- tens of square metres of coplanar co-facing surface, and exactly the pair check-coplanar catches.

colorMaterialRecipe.recipe: Grey deck membrane, roughness 0.93, seen only over the parapet.

actionProfile.notes: Rigidly parented to the root. NO pivot and NO socket, deliberately: this part does not move and nothing attaches to it.

componentTree.name: Parapet ring and fascia wall
componentTree.topologyRationale: A continuous upstand ring in one material, with the front simply taller -- which a plan extrusion cannot express, since an extrude carries one height. Merged boxes are the right primitive, and anything else in the same material folds in here rather than costing its own submission.

geometryDescriptor.topologyIntent: Front fascia wall (7.96 wide) plus left, right and rear upstands (outer faces at +-3.98 / -3.48, inboard of the band), plus the 0.10 m white coping strip over the band on three sides, merged into ONE component and ONE draw call.
geometryDescriptor.zFightingNote: Parapet outer faces stand 0.06 m PROUD of the shell walls. Authored flush they would be coplanar and co-facing along all three elevations. The front box overlaps into the shell volume rather than butting it.
geometryDescriptor.mergeNote: Primitive is "box" because the schema enumerates primitives, but this is a MERGED cluster built into one BufferGeometry and submitted as ONE draw call.

colorMaterialRecipe.recipe: The SAME render as the shell -- one material. Caps the rear volume at the declared height and is what hides the condensers from the street.

actionProfile.notes: Rigidly parented to the root. NO pivot and NO socket, deliberately: this part does not move and nothing attaches to it.

componentTree.name: Brand fascia panel
componentTree.topologyRationale: BoxGeometry lays its faces out as a known slice of the uv attribute, so one run can name the face that carries the graphic while its siblings sample a plain corner. That is what wraps a band round three sides at one draw call and one material.

geometryDescriptor.topologyIntent: Navy band 0.68 m tall (plate: 56 px navy over 238 px soffit height at the front-right corner, x=760) wrapping the whole roof edge -- the +Z run at the envelope plane and both side runs the FULL 6.84 m depth, as the plate's right elevation shows the band running to the rear block. Marked on +Z only.
geometryDescriptor.zFightingNote: Side runs stop at z=3.34, BEHIND the front run's back face at 3.33..3.49 -- run to the same depth they intersected it and the canvas smeared through the overlap. Their outer faces are the +-4.00 envelope plane, so the parapet upstands were moved inboard to +-3.98 and the fascia wall narrowed to 7.96, neither of which may share that plane.

localFeatures.description: ptt mark on the street-facing run
localFeatures.delivery: post-construction baked WebP (sign/compose.py), per-run face UV

colorMaterialRecipe.recipe: Navy acrylic band, roughness 0.42. THREE runs in one component and one material: the +Z run names the face that samples the mark canvas, the two side returns are flagged plain and sample a flat corner of it.
colorMaterialRecipe.postConstructionMap: SIGN_IMAGE_DATA_URL, a 2048x512 WebP (~10 KB) embedded in the bundle and loaded through TextureLoader, colour forced white. Composed once in Pillow (scratch/<id>/sign/compose.py): emblem = fal-ai/flux/dev droplet-flame with an inner hollow drop (seed 21, ~$0.03), a stylised approximation of the trademark and recorded as such, thresholded to a white mask at 80 % of the band height; wordmark = 'ptt' in Nimbus Sans Bold Italic at 62 % of the flame height. Mark 2.22 x 0.54 m, x 0.52..0.80 of the run (plate: 0.50..0.66 foreshortened, right of centre). Baked because the first ship's fillText flame glyph fell back to a stray dot; drawFallbackSign() vector paths remain as the decode-failure fallback.

actionProfile.notes: Rigidly parented to the root. NO pivot and NO socket, deliberately: this part does not move and nothing attaches to it.

componentTree.name: Shopfront glazing
componentTree.topologyRationale: One pane, not one per bay: the mullion grid in front does the dividing, and a pane per bay would cost a draw call each to express one sheet of glass.

geometryDescriptor.topologyIntent: Single tinted pane, overlapping INTO the facade at the back and RECESSED behind the framing at the front, which is what makes it read as glass set into a frame.
geometryDescriptor.zFightingNote: Front face sits behind the frame and mullion fronts; back face is inside the facade solid. No coincident face.

colorMaterialRecipe.recipe: Tinted pane, roughness 0.13, opacity 0.94. One wide pane under the canopy; the frame and mullions do the dividing.

actionProfile.notes: Rigidly parented to the root. NO pivot and NO socket, deliberately: this part does not move and nothing attaches to it.

componentTree.name: Shopfront framing and door bay
componentTree.topologyRationale: Every one of these parts is the same metal. Folding them into one component is the draw-call lever chosen in the BLOCKOUT -- a part split for authoring convenience cannot be merged afterwards once pivots hang off it.

geometryDescriptor.topologyIntent: Perimeter frame, transom, kick rail, door jambs and door header MERGED into one component.
geometryDescriptor.zFightingNote: Frame front face stands proud of both the glazing and the mullions. The frame OVERLAPS the glazing it holds rather than meeting its edge, which is the rule that stops a frame putting four coincident reveal faces in the model.
geometryDescriptor.mergeNote: Merged multi-box cluster, one BufferGeometry, one draw call.

colorMaterialRecipe.recipe: Mill-finish aluminium, metalness 0.25. Head, sill and two jambs merged into one geometry.

actionProfile.notes: Rigidly parented to the root. NO pivot and NO socket, deliberately: this part does not move and nothing attaches to it.

componentTree.name: Canopy slab and service door
componentTree.topologyRationale: Two parts in one render material, so the prop's largest single surface costs no extra shader switch.

geometryDescriptor.topologyIntent: The roof slab extending forward to z=3.48 over the apron, plus a flush service door standing proud of the +X wall.
geometryDescriptor.zFightingNote: The slab is 0.30 thick, not 0.32: at 0.32 its top face sat at y=3.620 with the roof deck's top face, coplanar and co-facing over 18.6 m2.

localFeatures.description: roof slab extending forward over the apron

colorMaterialRecipe.recipe: The canopy slab and the +X service door ride ONE component because both are the white render -- grouping by material rather than by location is what holds the draw calls down.

actionProfile.notes: Rigidly parented to the root. NO pivot and NO socket, deliberately: this part does not move and nothing attaches to it.

componentTree.name: Canopy columns
componentTree.topologyRationale: Two identical columns in one component; too few to earn an InstancedMesh against the geometry ceiling.

geometryDescriptor.topologyIntent: Two 0.34 m square columns at x=+-2.60, SYMMETRIC about the centreline, from the ground into the slab (0..3.40). The plate's pair is asymmetric (0.19 and 0.65 of the run); symmetric placement per user direction 2026-08-26.
geometryDescriptor.zFightingNote: Column tops sink into the slab rather than meeting its soffit plane.

colorMaterialRecipe.recipe: The two columns carry the shopfront FRAMING material, not the render: in the plate they are the same clad aluminium section as the shopfront jambs.

componentTree.topologyRationale: Three runs of the same stripe merged into one geometry.

geometryDescriptor.zFightingNote: Front run 7.96 wide at z 3.36..3.50, 1 cm proud of the band's front face at 3.49; side runs at +-3.99 outer, 1 cm inboard of the band plane.

colorMaterialRecipe.recipe: Red enamel stripe, roughness 0.50. Three runs, one material, one draw call.

featureReviews.evidence: Envelope built at exactly 8.00 x 4.60 x 7.00 m against the declared 8 x 4.6 x 7, with the enclosed volume at the REAR and the canopy taking the front 3.2 m.
featureReviews.notes: The setback is the whole prop: what reads as a separate awning is the building's own roof slab running forward on two columns, so the shell face is at z=0.30 rather than pushed forward like every sibling. Meshy reads the plate 43% deeper than the declared module -- the forecourt, which the plate frames as part of the object -- while agreeing on height within 4%. The kit's shared 7.0 m depth wins and the canopy is fitted inside it, so it keeps its proportion instead of being cropped. The red stripe overran to 7.01 m at its first depth and was caught by measurement, not by eye.

featureReviews.evidence: White flame glyph and italic 'ptt' on navy, right of centre on the street-facing run, with the red enamel stripe under the band on all three exposed edges.
featureReviews.notes: The band wraps three sides at ONE component and one material: the +Z run names the face that samples the canvas, the two returns are flagged plain and sample a flat corner of it. Two distinct faults had to be fixed before that held. The returns originally ran to the same depth as the front run and intersected it, smearing the canvas through the overlap; and `plain` was implemented as a sentinel slice index of -1, which still satisfied `i >= start && i < start+4` for vertices 0-2, so three corners of the +X face kept sampling the wordmark band. The test is now an explicit boolean. The flame is set as a typographic mark, not the corporate droplet -- the one part of this feature that is an approximation rather than a match.

lodPlan.strategy: full component tree and material layers
merge static components and reduce local feature geometry

performanceBudget.optimizationPolicy: Real-time browser FPS prop on low-end integrated GPUs; a level builder places hundreds at once. All four ceilings come from thaikit resolveBudget() for the hero2x class and none was invented. The component split was costed against the DRAW-CALL ceiling in the blockout, before any geometry existed: parts that share a material are merged into one component rather than left to be merged later, because a pivot hung off a part cannot be merged afterwards.

drawCalls.note: Two repetition systems collapse 7 parts into 2 submissions. The navy band wraps three sides at ONE component and one material by naming the face each run samples, and the canopy slab shares its component with the service door because both are the render.

materials.note: wall covers shell, parapet, canopy slab and service door; frame covers the shopfront framing, the mullions AND the two columns, which are the same clad section in the plate. Seven of eight materials, one in hand.

uniqueGeometries.note: One per component plus one per repetition system. A scaled box is NOT a shared geometry -- the generator bakes real dimensions in via geometry.scale(), so every differently-sized box is genuinely distinct. Each InstancedMesh reuses a single geometry across all its instances, which is the whole point.

triangles.note: Triangles are NOT the binding constraint on this prop -- draw calls are. The headroom is deliberately spent on silhouette quality (chamfers, cowl segments, shutter ribs) and must not be read as room to split components, which would spend the axis that is actually scarce.

lightingFromPhoto.notes: The plate is a flat studio lightbox: surfaces at 90 degrees to each other measure within a few levels, which is only possible under near-shadowless illumination. That is WHY the measured crop means are usable as albedo with little correction.
High fill ratio inferred from the shadow-side wall retaining full value.

The seamless backdrop acts as a large uniform environment. The thaikit harness supplies NO environment map, which is why every metal on this prop carries a metalness well below its physical value -- a metal with nothing to reflect renders black.
NO rim light in the plate. Recorded so a missing rim in the render is not read as a defect.
Exposure 1.0 with ACES filmic tone mapping; no exposure compensation is applied to the measured albedos and none is warranted.

NO contact or ground shadow in the plate -- it is a cut-out against a seamless backdrop. Recorded so the absence is not read as a missing feature. IN USE this is a floor-placed building and the HOST scene owns its contact shadow: castShadow ships enabled on every mesh and the factory defines no ground plane of its own.

proceduralStrategy.strategy: box, cylinder and merged-box clusters only. No organic surfaces exist on this subject.
Two InstancedMesh systems carry 7 of the 21 discrete parts.
All procedural variation is assigned by instance INDEX, never from a random source, so the model is byte-identical on every build.

Every material is declared textureless. The brand fascia receives its wordmark as a generated canvas assigned AFTER material construction -- the documented route for a printed brand fascia, unaffected by the declaration.

risks.description: Meshy reads this plate 43% deeper than the declared module, because the plate frames the forecourt canopy and its apron as part of the object.
risks.mitigation: The declared 7.0 m is the kit's shared retail depth and wins. The canopy is fitted inside it at 3.2 m by setting the shell back to z=0.30, so the canopy keeps its proportion instead of being cropped. Height agrees within 4%.

risks.description: The glazing ships at #6F7477 rather than its measured #454A4B.
risks.mitigation: Forced by a luma-only background test: at the measured value the pane composited to the backdrop and the shopfront was read as a hole. Recorded with the measurement it departs from.

risks.description: Pumps, apron and paving are absent, though the plate shows the building as part of a forecourt.
risks.mitigation: Deliberate: this asset is the kiosk and its canopy. The apron is the level builder's ground plane, and pumps are separate props.
